answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small, time-locked bond before it may trade, like laying a basalt foundation under every shopfront. The bond is slashed if peers prove the identity faked work, and released only after a long horizon of honest behavior, so creating thousands of fake agents costs real capital up front. Copper-grade reputation then accrues slowly per verified transaction, so an attacker cannot buy instant trust, while honest newcomers still join cheaply by staking one bond and earning standing over time.
